# Apply Fixes

## Change Summary

Normalized periphyton and decomposer habitat maps on every `refresh_habitat_registry` call so legacy/changed states are redistributed onto currently valid habitats instead of retaining biomass on removed filter/plant/substrate habitats; also stopped treating `SubstrateDeep` as a valid periphyton target. Reworked decomposer decay bookkeeping so DOC/DON routing is based on the biomass actually removed from habitat pools, including the zero-DO uneven-pool fallback. Replaced proportional shrimp/microfauna periphyton removal with habitat-accessibility-weighted grazing that favors exposed glass/substrate surfaces over filter media, and expanded habitat biomass regressions to cover habitat removal, weighted grazing, and zero-DO decay conservation.

## Steps

1. [Completed] Inspected the reported habitat-pool refresh, decomposer decay, and grazing code paths to confirm how biomass maps, decay routing, and grazing were currently behaving.
2. [Completed] Patched habitat-pool normalization in state/biology, added accessibility-weighted periphyton removal for shrimp and microfauna, and made decomposer decay route only the biomass actually removed from habitat pools.
3. [Completed] Expanded habitat biomass regressions for removed habitats, weighted grazing, and zero-DO decay conservation, then ran targeted validation across habitat, save/load, shrimp, and microfauna tests.

## Validation Evidence

- `cargo test -p tank_core --test habitat_biomass_pools` passed (13 tests).
- `cargo test -p tank_core --test shrimp_feeding_pathway --test microfauna_routing --test save_load` passed.
- `cargo test -p tank_core shrimp_feeding_` passed the affected shrimp unit tests.
- `cargo test -p tank_core update_condition_treats_full_accessible_ration_as_satiated` passed.

## Outstanding Risks

- Validation covered targeted `tank_core` tests only; the full workspace test suite was not run.
